en: Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the ground, preventing slips when running on a wet basketball court.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water conducts electricity and can cause a dangerous shock.
Wrapping an ice pack in a towel prevents direct heat transfer that could freeze and damage your skin.
Using a wheelbarrow, a second-class lever, lets you lift heavy garden soil with much less physical effort.
Swallowing small neodymium magnets is dangerous because they attract each other inside your intestines and cause severe tissue tears.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light rays that can permanently damage the sensitive lenses of your eyes.
Listening to headphones at maximum volume for over an hour can permanently damage the tiny hair cells inside your ears.
Wearing a helmet protects your brain from the strong downward pull of gravity if you accidentally fall off your bicycle.
The thermal energy from a hot stove burner causes severe skin burns if you touch it without thick oven mitts.
Pushing a heavy box up a ramp requires less force than lifting it straight up into the back of a truck.
Overloading a single extension cord with too many plugs generates excess heat energy that can easily start an electrical fire.
Rubbing your hands together quickly generates heat energy through friction, which safely warms your skin on a cold rainy day.
